item.title: IFA members continue protest at Bord Bia in Dublin
item.description: IFA members are planning to continue protesting at Bord Bia in Dublin today. They will demonstrate both inside and outside the building in anger over the Chair of the company Larry Murrin importing some Brazilian beef. 6 members of the Irish Farmers Association held a sit-down protest inside Bord Bia yesterday despite repeatedly being asked to leave. item.title: Local rep calls for improved access to education for special needs children
item.description: A Co Monaghan woman has outlined the challenges faced by parents and carers of children with special needs. Local Aontú representative Olivia Larkin is part of Special Needs Active Parents which campaigns for improved special needs services in Monaghan. Olivia says parents are waiting on an activation unit for children coming out of secondary school aged 18, an increase in respite services and additional special school places. item.title: Over 700 new cars registered across region
item.description: Cavan and Monaghan have seen very little change in the number of new cars registered in January compared to the same time last year. That's according to figures released by the Society of the Irish Motor Industry recently. There have been 411 new cars registered in Cavan in January of this year. This compares to 409 registered in the same month in 2025. This is a 0.49% change. In Monaghan the figure for January 2026 stands at 303, compared with 304 at the same time last year. item.title: Cavan resident says new legislation for landlords has been her 'downfall'
item.description: A Co Cavan resident says the new planned legislation for landlords is the reason why she is facing homelessness. Rebecca Lambe who has lived in Virginia for the last 10 years says she received an eviction notice before Christmas. She says the purposed legislation from the government that radically alters the market for tenants and landlords has been her downfall and she says others will be in the same position.
